how_to_get: The application text is /mnt/project-files/data-requests/radiopaedia-application-draft.md (the thread's file); the agreement is SignNow document 2b7a4819d4ea45198cd8e71ba0703993ba89663b, sent to andrew.murphy+ml@radiopaedia.org with license@radiopaedia.org in copy.

Approved: agreement ID 202610-9517, countersigned 2026-10-23 and received 2026-10-26. The cases are collected by hand from the site at a gentle rate (clause 3): Radiopaedia supplies no export and no DICOM, and the site refuses scripted requests (HTTP 406, 2026-10-31), so this project never fetches Radiopaedia by script unless Radiopaedia allowlists a named client; a request that it do so was drafted for the owner on 2026-10-31. For the owner's tiers of 2026-10-27 a case is a few key images, mostly of part of the spine: a case whose image carries its author's drawn level label, or an arrow its caption names by level, is silver 3 (gold 3 for a whole-spine film or CT), and a case that names its level only in the text is report-only, silver 4 (gold 4); each case is read when it is collected, and nothing is held until then.
A commercial product built from any model that touched these cases needs a negotiated licence first (clause 2b).

Saved images are laid out as <group>/<rID>/*.jpg (group fluoro or xr) and arranged by `python3 tools/radiopaedia_import.py run --from <saved> --to <out>` for grid/banks/radiopaedia_fluoro.json and radiopaedia_xr.json; the folder reaches the grid as a carried folder (grid/carry/README.md), then bank, ingest, and the leak check against every held shard before any frame enters a test split.
